## Purpose

This SOP describes the bioinformatics workflow for processing amplicon
sequencing data (16S rRNA, ITS, 18S rRNA) from raw demultiplexed FASTQ
files through quality filtering, denoising, taxonomic classification,
and generation of analysis-ready feature tables. The pipeline uses
QIIME 2 as the primary framework with DADA2 as the denoising algorithm
[@bolyen2019; @callahan2016]. DADA2 resolves amplicon sequence variants
(ASVs) at single-nucleotide resolution, replacing the older OTU-clustering
approach with a more reproducible and sensitive method [@callahan2017].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Processing of Illumina paired-end amplicon sequencing
  data (MiSeq, NextSeq) for 16S, ITS, and 18S marker genes generated
  from EA Program environmental samples
- **Does not apply to:** Shotgun metagenomics; long-read sequencing
  (PacBio, Nanopore); transcriptomics (RNA-seq); ddPCR data analysis
  (see [SOP-L702](SOP-L702-ddpcr-data-analysis.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program lab computers or personal workstations with
  QIIME 2 installed; high-performance computing cluster if available


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve pipeline parameters and taxonomy database |
| Trained Personnel | Run the pipeline per this SOP; document all parameters |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent analysis |


## Software Requirements

| Software              | Version (minimum) | Notes                          |
|:----------------------|:------------------|:-------------------------------|
| QIIME 2               | 2024.2 or later   | Install via conda/mamba; see <https://docs.qiime2.org> |
| DADA2 (QIIME 2 plugin) | Bundled with QIIME 2 | R package also available for standalone use |
| R and RStudio         | R 4.3+            | For downstream statistical analysis; see [SOP-L801](SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd) |
| phyloseq (R package)  | 1.44+             | For importing QIIME 2 artifacts into R [@mcmurdie2013] |
| FastQC                | 0.12+             | Optional; for initial read quality inspection |

Install QIIME 2 in a dedicated conda environment to avoid dependency
conflicts:

```bash
# Example installation (check docs.qiime2.org for current commands)
conda env create -n qiime2-2024.2 \
  --file https://data.qiime2.org/distro/amplicon/qiime2-amplicon-2024.2-py39-linux-conda.yml
conda activate qiime2-2024.2
```


## Procedure

### Data Organization

1. Create a project directory with the following structure:

```
project_name/
├── raw_data/          # Demultiplexed FASTQ files from sequencing facility
├── qiime2/            # QIIME 2 artifacts and visualizations
├── results/           # Exported tables, trees, taxonomy
├── scripts/           # Shell and R scripts
└── metadata/          # Sample metadata TSV file
```

2. Prepare a sample metadata file (`metadata.tsv`) in tab-separated
   format. The first column must be `sample-id` matching the FASTQ
   filenames. Include all experimental variables (site, treatment, date,
   depth, replicate). Validate the file at
   <https://keemei.qiime2.org/> [@rideout2016].

### Import Raw Reads

Import demultiplexed paired-end FASTQ files into a QIIME 2 artifact:

```bash
qiime tools import \
  --type 'SampleData[PairedEndSequencesWithQuality]' \
  --input-path raw_data/ \
  --input-format CasavaOneEightSingleLanePerSampleDirFmt \
  --output-path qiime2/demux.qza
```

Visualize read quality:

```bash
qiime demux summarize \
  --i-data qiime2/demux.qza \
  --o-visualization qiime2/demux-summary.qzv
```

Open `demux-summary.qzv` at <https://view.qiime2.org> to inspect
quality score profiles. Use these plots to determine truncation
parameters for DADA2 (Section 5.3).

### Denoising with DADA2

DADA2 performs quality filtering, chimera removal, and denoising in a
single step, producing an ASV feature table and representative sequences
[@callahan2016].

```bash
qiime dada2 denoise-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-seqs qiime2/demux.qza \
  --p-trunc-len-f 240 \
  --p-trunc-len-r 200 \
  --p-trim-left-f 0 \
  --p-trim-left-r 0 \
  --p-n-threads 4 \
  --o-table qiime2/table.qza \
  --o-representative-sequences qiime2/rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-denoising-stats qiime2/dada2-stats.qza
```

::: {.callout-important}
### Setting Truncation Parameters

Choose `--p-trunc-len-f` and `--p-trunc-len-r` based on the quality
plots from Section 5.2. Truncate where the median quality score drops
below 25--30. The forward and reverse reads must still overlap by at
least 20 bp after truncation for successful merging. For 16S V4
(515F/806R, ~290 bp amplicon) with 2x250 reads, typical values are
240 (forward) and 200 (reverse).
:::

Review denoising statistics:

```bash
qiime metadata tabulate \
  --m-input-file qiime2/dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-visualization qiime2/dada2-stats.qzv
```

Check the percentage of reads passing each filter step (input, filtered,
denoised, merged, non-chimeric). A healthy run retains > 60% of input
reads through the full pipeline.

### Taxonomic Classification

Assign taxonomy to ASVs using a pre-trained Naive Bayes classifier.
Download the appropriate classifier from the QIIME 2 Data Resources
page (<https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.2/data-resources/>).

**For 16S (SILVA 138.1):**

```bash
qiime feature-classifier classify-sklearn \
  --i-classifier silva-138.1-ssu-nr99-515f-806r-classifier.qza \
  --i-reads qiime2/rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-classification qiime2/taxonomy.qza
```

**For ITS (UNITE):**

```bash
qiime feature-classifier classify-sklearn \
  --i-classifier unite-ver9-dynamic-all-29.11.2022-classifier.qza \
  --i-reads qiime2/rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-classification qiime2/taxonomy.qza
```

Visualize taxonomy:

```bash
qiime taxa barplot \
  --i-table qiime2/table.qza \
  --i-taxonomy qiime2/taxonomy.qza \
  --m-metadata-file metadata/metadata.tsv \
  --o-visualization qiime2/taxa-barplot.qzv
```

### Phylogenetic Tree Construction

Build a rooted phylogenetic tree for diversity analyses:

```bash
qiime phylogeny align-to-tree-mafft-fasttree \
  --i-sequences qiime2/rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-alignment qiime2/aligned-rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-masked-alignment qiime2/masked-aligned-rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-tree qiime2/unrooted-tree.qza \
  --o-rooted-tree qiime2/rooted-tree.qza
```

### Filtering

Remove contaminant ASVs identified in negative controls, mitochondrial
and chloroplast sequences, and low-frequency ASVs:

```bash
# Remove mitochondria and chloroplast
qiime taxa filter-table \
  --i-table qiime2/table.qza \
  --i-taxonomy qiime2/taxonomy.qza \
  --p-exclude mitochondria,chloroplast \
  --o-filtered-table qiime2/table-filtered.qza

# Remove low-frequency ASVs (e.g., singletons)
qiime feature-table filter-features \
  --i-table qiime2/table-filtered.qza \
  --p-min-frequency 2 \
  --o-filtered-table qiime2/table-final.qza
```

For decontamination using negative control data, export the feature
table to R and use the `decontam` package [@davis2018].

### Export for R Analysis

Export QIIME 2 artifacts for downstream analysis in R with phyloseq
[@mcmurdie2013]:

```bash
qiime tools export \
  --input-path qiime2/table-final.qza \
  --output-path results/

qiime tools export \
  --input-path qiime2/taxonomy.qza \
  --output-path results/

qiime tools export \
  --input-path qiime2/rooted-tree.qza \
  --output-path results/
```

Alternatively, import QIIME 2 artifacts directly into R using the
`qiime2R` package.


## Quality Control

- Inspect the DADA2 denoising stats for every run. Flag samples with
  fewer than 1,000 reads after denoising.
- Verify that negative controls (NTC, extraction blank) contain fewer
  than 100 reads. If controls contain substantial reads, use `decontam`
  to identify and remove contaminant ASVs [@davis2018; @salter2014].
- Confirm that the positive control (mock community) recovers the
  expected taxa at the expected relative abundances.
- Document all QIIME 2 and DADA2 parameters in the project README and
  in the analysis scripts. Reproducibility requires recording the exact
  software versions, classifier version, and truncation lengths.
- Archive raw FASTQ files, the QIIME 2 artifacts, and the analysis
  scripts in the project GitHub repository per
  [SOP-L801](SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd).

## Training Record

Before running the bioinformatics pipeline independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete the QIIME 2 "Moving Pictures" tutorial
   (<https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.2/tutorials/moving-pictures/>)
3. Process a test dataset under supervision, from import through
   taxonomy assignment and export to R
4. Demonstrate correct interpretation of DADA2 denoising statistics and
   quality plots
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
